title: Cohomology via a weakly contractible hypercover
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $a\in\mathbf Z$. Let $W_\bullet\to U$ be a hypercovering of an object $U$ of this site (the matching-cover condition of [det-pe-hypercover-existence]), with each $W_r$ weakly contractible [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of sheaves of $\mathcal R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with $K^b=0$ for $b<a$. Put $C^{r,b}=K^b(W_r)$ for $r\geq0$, with horizontal differential $\delta=\sum_{i=0}^{r+1}(-1)^id_i^*:C^{r,b}\to C^{r+1,b}$ and signed vertical differential $(-1)^rd_K:C^{r,b}\to C^{r,b+1}$. Set $\operatorname{Tot}(C)^q=\bigoplus_{r+b=q,\ r\geq0}C^{r,b}=\bigoplus_{0\leq r\leq q-a}K^{q-r}(W_r)$, with differential $\delta+(-1)^rd_K$. Let $R\Gamma(U,-)$ mean the right derived functor of the additive section functor $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R)\to\mathbf{Ab}$, $F\mapsto F(U)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Then there is an isomorphism $R\Gamma(U,K^\bullet)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}(C)$ in the derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], natural in $K^\bullet$.

proof.text: For $r\geq0$, the naturality of $d_K$ makes it commute with all face pullbacks, and the simplicial identities pair the terms of $\delta^2$ with opposite signs. Thus the unsigned horizontal and vertical differentials commute and each squares to zero. On $C^{r,b}$ the two mixed terms in the square of the signed total differential are $(-1)^{r+1}d_K\delta$ and $(-1)^r\delta d_K$, which cancel. If $r+b=q$ and $b\geq a$, then $0\leq r\leq q-a$. This proves the asserted finite direct-sum formula, including zero when $q<a$. A coefficient chain map acts on every summand by its map on sections and therefore defines a functor $T(K)=\operatorname{Tot}(K^b(W_r))$.

source.place: Tag 09A2 (lemma-compute-cohomology), total complex; explicit signs and finite diagonals as in blueprint Finiteness

proof.text: Evaluation at every $W_r$ is exact, without requiring affineness. Work in the $\mathcal V$-small skeleton of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (see step 3), on which every presheaf of abelian groups has a sheafification, as that definition already uses for the constant sheaf $A_Y$; this is the site hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Indeed [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] describes kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying the sectionwise cokernels, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] states that forgetting the module structure preserves both kernels and cokernels. Thus the underlying abelian-sheaf functor is exact. A module epimorphism is therefore an epimorphism of abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] it is locally surjective, and by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] its underlying set-sheaf morphism is epi. The weak-contractibility property [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible] makes its evaluation at $W_r$ surjective. Hence evaluation preserves kernels and epimorphisms, so is exact. For any complex $E$, apply exact evaluation to $0\to Z^b(E)\to E^b\to B^{b+1}(E)\to0$ and $0\to B^b(E)\to Z^b(E)\to H^b(E)\to0$. The resulting kernel and quotient identify $H^b(E(W_r))$ with $H^b(E)(W_r)$, functorially in $E$. Thus evaluation preserves cohomology and in particular carries every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09A2 (lemma-compute-cohomology), exact evaluation; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA; sites.tex Tag 00WN

proof.text: Use throughout the $\mathcal V$-small skeleton stipulated in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with all coefficient and derived categories formed in $\mathcal V$. Clause 3 of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site] supplies essential smallness in this larger universe; no essential-smallness assertion in the smaller scheme universe is needed. Choose $s:K\to I$ by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution], applied to this small ringed site. Thus $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $I$ is bounded below, every $I^b$ is an injective module sheaf, and $I$ is K-injective. Let $c$ be any lower bound for $I$, and put $N=\min(a,c)$; no assertion that the resolution has exactly the original lower bound is needed. The right derived functor $R\Gamma(U,-)$ of the statement exists: on this $\mathcal V$-small site, $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] (no commutativity of $\mathcal R$ is assumed there), so by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] every complex, bounded or not, has a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex; this is the standing hypothesis of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. By [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], the K-injective resolution computes $R\Gamma(U,K)$ as the complex $I(U)$.

source.place: Tag 09A2 (lemma-compute-cohomology), second paragraph: choose a bounded-below injective resolution; derived.tex Tags 05TI and 070I

proof.text: The pro-étale covering precoverage on the small skeleton contains isomorphisms, is stable under composition and base change, and admits the covering pullbacks; it is subcanonical by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. For any compatible family of lower simplices over $T\to U$, the matching universal property gives a map $T$ to the matching object. Pulling back the hypercover matching covering along that map gives local lifts to $W_n$. In degree zero this is just the pullback of $W_0\to U$. These verify exactly the local-matching hypothesis of [lem-sc-ringed-hypercover-injective-augmentation-ring]. Apply that theorem with ring sheaf $\mathcal R$, base object $U$, simplicial object $W_\bullet$, and injective module $I^b$. It gives the exact augmented row $0\to I^b(U)\to I^b(W_0)\to I^b(W_1)\to\cdots$ for every $b$, with the stated alternating restriction maps. The module coefficient category is used throughout; injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf is never required.

source.place: Tags 01GE (lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves) and 01GW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech); ringed-module version of the free-sheaf/injective-Hom argument

proof.text: For every coefficient complex $E$, define $\alpha_E:E(U)\to T(E)$ by restriction to $W_0$, inserted in total bidegree $(0,b)$ in degree $b$. The two face restrictions to $W_1$ agree because both augment to $U$, so their alternating difference vanishes. Restriction commutes with $d_E$, and the vertical sign at $r=0$ is $1$, so $\alpha_E$ is a chain map, natural in $E$. With $E=I$, put $A=I(U)$ and use the bicomplex $D^{r,b}=I^b(W_r)$ extended by zero for $r<0$. It and $A$ vanish below $b=N$. Step 4 says precisely that the maps from $I^b(U)[0]$ to the fixed-$b$ rows are quasi-isomorphisms. The outgoing horizontal differential kills the column-zero augmentation, as just checked. The abelian category of abelian groups has countable coproducts (coordinatewise direct sums). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-row-augmentation] applies and gives that $\alpha_I:I(U)\to T(I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09A2 (lemma-compute-cohomology), final paragraph; homology.tex Tags 0132 (lemma-first-quadrant-ss) and 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution)

proof.text: By step 2, evaluation takes $s:K\to I$ to a quasi-isomorphism $K(W_r)\to I(W_r)$ for every $r$. Both section bicomplexes vanish for $r<0$ or $b<N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-total-column-comparison] with common bounds $P=0$ and $Q=N$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $T(s):T(K)\to T(I)$. For any quasi-isomorphism $u:E\to F$ between bounded-below coefficient complexes, choose lower bounds $e,f$ and put $B=\min(e,f)$. Step 2 makes each column map $E(W_r)\to F(W_r)$ a quasi-isomorphism, and both bicomplexes vanish for $r<0$ or $b<B$. The cited column-comparison theorem with $P=0,Q=B$ therefore makes $T(u)$ a quasi-isomorphism. In the derived category the composite $R\Gamma(U,K)\simeq I(U)\xrightarrow{\alpha_I}T(I)\xrightarrow{T(s)^{-1}}T(K)$ is therefore an isomorphism and has exactly the total complex stated in the item.

We verify naturality and independence of the resolution rather than merely choosing isomorphisms objectwise. For a chain map $f:K\to L$ and resolutions $s:K\to I$, $t:L\to J$ chosen as in step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied with source $I$ and target $J$, lifts the derived map $(Qt)(Qf)(Qs)^{-1}:QI\to QJ$ to a chain map $g:I\to J$, unique up to homotopy. Applying the injectivity of the same Hom bijection with source $K$ and target $J$ to $Q(gs)=Q(tf)$ gives $gs\simeq tf$. The functor $T$ preserves chain homotopies: if $h:E^b\to F^{b-1}$ is a coefficient homotopy, take on the summand of horizontal degree $r$ the total homotopy $(-1)^rh(W_r)$. Writing $u-v=d_Fh+hd_E$ for the coefficient homotopy equation, the vertical part of $d_{T(F)}H+Hd_{T(E)}$ on horizontal degree $r$ is $(-1)^r(-1)^r(d_Fh+hd_E)=u-v$. Its horizontal part is $(-1)^r\delta_Fh+(-1)^{r+1}h\delta_E=0$, since $h$ commutes with every restriction. Thus $dH+Hd=T(u)-T(v)$. Hence $T(g)T(s)=T(t)T(f)$ in the derived category. Naturality of restriction gives $T(g)\alpha_I=\alpha_Jg(U)$. These two equalities and inversion of $T(s),T(t)$ show that the isomorphisms of step 6 commute with $f$ and $R\Gamma(U,f)$, the latter being $g(U)$ under the K-injective computation [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Taking $f=\mathrm{id}$ gives independence of the chosen resolution. Since step 6 inverts quasi-isomorphisms, the same naturality passes to derived morphisms.

Second reading expanded the arbitrary quasi-isomorphism comparison, the two K-injective Hom applications, and the signed total-homotopy equation; no new nodes or changed hypotheses.

In step 5 the row-augmentation hypotheses hold, with δ∘a=0 and common bound N. Step 6 is a correct column comparison with P=0, Q=N. Step 7 is sound: g is lifted through the K-injective Hom bijection, the homotopy (−1)^r h(W_r) is correct, and compatibility with RΓ(U,f) follows from naturality of the unit η.
